learn.hook: Is there a magic trick that turns a tiny seed into a mango tree overnight? Let's find out!
points: The lesson 'A Bottle of Dew' is a story about wanting quick success and learning the value of hard work.
A shortcut promises fast results with little effort; hard work means steady effort over time.
To understand a story, ask: Who is in it? What do they want? What problem do they face? How does it end?
The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches. We find it by looking at what happens to the characters because of their choices.
Read every question carefully and look back at the passage for the exact words that prove your answer.

example.q: Read this passage: Meera wanted the best mangoes in the village. Her friend Kabir said, "Just buy a magic powder and the tree will fruit overnight!" Meera shook her head. Every morning she watered her little tree, pulled out weeds and added compost. Two summers later, her tree gave sweet, golden mangoes, and she shared them with everyone. What lesson does the story teach?
steps: Meera's goal: to grow the best mangoes.
Kabir offers a shortcut: a 'magic powder'.
Meera chooses steady work: watering, weeding and adding compost every day.
Result: after two summers, her tree gives sweet mangoes.
So the story shows that patient hard work brings real results.
example.answer: Patient, steady hard work brings real success; shortcuts rarely do.

learn.reallife: Practising cricket in the nets every evening, or revising a little every day before exams, works better than hoping for a last-minute trick.

games.title: True or false: Meera's story
items: Kabir suggested a magic powder.
Kabir said, 'Just buy a magic powder.'
Meera bought the magic powder.
Meera shook her head and chose to work hard instead.
Meera watered her tree every morning.
The passage says she watered it every morning.
The tree gave mangoes the very next day.
It gave mangoes two summers later.
Meera shared her mangoes with everyone.
The last line says she shared them with everyone.

games.title: Story sequence
games.prompt: Put Meera's story in the order it happened
items: Meera wants the best mangoes in the village.
Kabir suggests a magic powder.
Meera says no to the shortcut.
She waters, weeds and adds compost every day.
Her tree gives sweet, golden mangoes.

quiz.q: Meera's story begins: "Meera wanted the best mangoes in the village. Her friend Kabir said, 'Just buy a magic powder!'" What did Meera want?
options: The best mangoes in the village
quiz.explain: The first line says Meera wanted the best mangoes in the village.
quiz.mistake: Confuses what Kabir offered with what Meera wanted

quiz.q: In Meera's story, Kabir said, "Just buy a magic powder and the tree will fruit overnight!" What is Kabir suggesting?
quiz.explain: A powder that works 'overnight' promises quick results with no effort, which is a shortcut.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that 'overnight' means 'very quickly, without effort'

quiz.q: Meera "watered her little tree, pulled out weeds and added compost" every morning. This shows that Meera was:
quiz.explain: Doing the same useful work every day shows patience and hard work.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect actions in the story with the character's qualities

quiz.q: In the story, Meera's tree gave mangoes "two summers later". What does this tell us?
options: Good results can take a long time
Mango trees grow in one night
quiz.explain: Two summers is a long time, so real results came slowly.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Kabir's promise with what really happened

quiz.q: What is the moral of Meera's mango story?
options: Steady hard work brings real success
quiz.explain: Meera worked patiently and got sweet mangoes, so the story praises steady effort.
quiz.mistake: Picks a detail from the story instead of the lesson it teaches

quiz.q: Which word from Meera's story means 'very quickly, by the next morning'?
quiz.explain: Kabir promised the tree would fruit 'overnight', meaning by the next morning.
quiz.mistake: Picks a time word without checking its exact meaning

quiz.q: Meera "shared them with everyone". What does this show about her?
quiz.explain: Sharing your mangoes with everyone is a generous act.
quiz.mistake: Does not link sharing with the quality of generosity

quiz.q: Which is the best title for Meera's story?
quiz.explain: The story is about patient work leading to sweet mangoes, so 'Sweet Fruit of Patience' sums it up.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a title based on a small detail rather than the main idea

teach.ask: Gappu flaps his wings: 'Why not just use a shortcut? Why did Meera work so hard on her tree?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Slow and steady effort gives real results. I'll practise my flying every day!
teach.nudge: But what did Meera get in the end because of her effort?

learn.hook: Words like 'honest', 'patient' and 'greedy' are tiny labels that tell us what a person is really like inside.
points: Values are good qualities that guide how we behave: honesty, patience, kindness, hard work, sharing.
Synonyms are words with similar meanings: hard-working = diligent; patient = calm while waiting.
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings: honest ↔ dishonest, patient ↔ impatient, generous ↔ selfish.
The prefixes 'un-', 'im-' and 'dis-' can make opposites: kind → unkind, patient → impatient, honest → dishonest.
We judge characters by what they say and do, not just by what they are called.

example.q: Think it through: Arjun finds a ₹100 note in the school corridor and hands it to his teacher. Which value does he show, and what is its opposite?
steps: Arjun does not keep money that isn't his.

learn.reallife: When you return a friend's lost pencil box or wait calmly in the lunch queue, you are showing values in action.

games.title: Good value or not?
buckets: Does not show a good value
items: waiting your turn calmly
sharing your tiffin
copying a friend's homework
telling the truth
grabbing the biggest piece
practising every day
blaming others for your mistake
helping a classmate

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym of 'hard-working'?
quiz.explain: 'Diligent' means working carefully and steadily, just like 'hard-working'.
quiz.mistake: Picks an antonym instead of a synonym

quiz.q: What is the antonym of 'patient'?
quiz.explain: We add the prefix 'im-' to 'patient' to make 'impatient'.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong prefix to form the opposite

quiz.q: Choose the opposite of 'honest'.
quiz.explain: The opposite of 'honest' is formed with 'dis-': dishonest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every word takes 'un-' to make its opposite

quiz.q: Riya gives half of her laddoos to a friend who forgot his tiffin. Which value does she show?
quiz.explain: Giving away part of what you have to help someone is generosity.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a good value with a bad quality

quiz.q: Which sentence shows patience?
options: Sonu pushed others to get on the swing.
Sonu shouted because the swing was busy.
Sonu broke the swing in anger.
Sonu waited calmly for his turn on the swing.
quiz.explain: Waiting calmly for your turn is what patience means.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the action with the value of patience

quiz.q: Which word is the antonym of 'generous'?
quiz.explain: A generous person shares; a selfish person keeps everything for himself or herself.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a synonym instead of the opposite

quiz.q: Which prefix makes the opposite of 'kind'?
quiz.explain: 'Kind' becomes 'unkind'. 'Re-' means 'again', not 'not'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'dis-' or 're-' without checking the real word

quiz.q: A 'shortcut' in a story usually means:
options: a quick, easy way that skips the real effort
quiz.explain: In stories about hard work, a shortcut is a way to get results quickly without doing the work.
quiz.mistake: Takes only the literal meaning of the word

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: 'What are values? And how do I make the opposite of a word like honest?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Values are good qualities, and little prefixes like 'dis-' and 'un-' flip a word into its opposite!
teach.nudge: And how can I turn 'honest' into its opposite word?

topics.title: Telling a story in the simple past

learn.hook: Most stories begin with 'Once upon a time...' and then the verbs travel back in time!
points: Stories usually use the simple past tense because they tell about things that already happened.
Regular verbs add -ed or -d: walk → walked, water → watered, smile → smiled.
Irregular verbs change in their own way: go → went, buy → bought, give → gave, see → saw.
Negative: did not + base verb ('She did not buy the powder', not 'did not bought').
Question: Did + subject + base verb ('Did Meera work hard?').

example.q: Think it through: Change to the simple past: 'Meera waters the tree and Kabir buys a powder.'
example.answer: Meera watered the tree and Kabir bought a powder.

learn.reallife: When you tell your family what happened at school today, you naturally use the past tense: 'We played kho-kho.'

items.text: Yesterday Ravi ___ his grandmother in Jaipur.
Meera did not ___ the magic powder.
Last Diwali, we ___ diyas on the balcony.
___ you finish your homework last night?
The tree ___ sweet mangoes two summers later.

quiz.q: What is the simple past of 'carry'?
quiz.explain: For verbs ending in consonant + y, change y to i and add -ed: carry → carried.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed without changing y to i

quiz.q: What is the simple past of 'buy'?
quiz.explain: 'Buy' is irregular: buy → bought. 'Brought' is the past of 'bring'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'bought' (buy) and 'brought' (bring)

quiz.q: Which negative sentence in the past tense is correct?
options: She did not took the shortcut.
She did not take the shortcut.
She did not taken the shortcut.
quiz.explain: After 'did not' we use the base verb: did not take.
quiz.mistake: Uses the past form after 'did'

quiz.q: Which verb is irregular?
quiz.explain: 'Go' becomes 'went'; the others just add -ed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every verb adds -ed in the past

quiz.q: Fill in: Last year, our class ___ a trip to the zoo.
quiz.explain: 'Last year' tells us the action is in the past, so we use 'made'.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the time clue 'last year'

quiz.q: Change to a question: 'Kabir sold the powder.'
quiz.explain: Questions in the simple past use 'Did' + subject + base verb.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the past form 'sold' after 'Did'

quiz.q: What is the simple past of 'stop'?
quiz.explain: Short verbs ending in one vowel + one consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the final consonant

quiz.q: Which time word tells you to use the simple past?
quiz.explain: 'Yesterday' points to the past. 'Tomorrow' and 'next week' are future; 'every day' is a habit.
quiz.mistake: Does not use time words as tense clues

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'I want to tell you what I did yesterday, but I keep saying I fly and I eat! How do I talk about the past?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Yesterday I flew, I ate and I learned the past tense!
teach.nudge: What about verbs like 'go' that don't just add -ed?
